q: Discuss the role of mycorrhizae in forest ecosystems and their significance for afforestation programmes in India.
a: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic associations between fungi and plant roots. Ectomycorrhizae (pine, oak) and endomycorrhizae (AM fungi) increase phosphorus and water uptake, protect roots from pathogens and improve soil structure through glomalin. In forests they form common mycorrhizal networks that transfer carbon and nutrients between trees. In India, nursery inoculation with Pisolithus and Glomus raises survival of seedlings in degraded lands, as seen in afforestation under the Green India Mission. Conclusion: mycorrhizal inoculation is a low-cost tool for restoration.
